children: J.B. Hunt Transport Services reported a higher year-over-year profit in the third quarter, despite a steep rise in operating expenses.

The logistics company's profit came in at $172.4 million, or $1.82 a share. That compares with a profit of $170.8 million, or $1.76 a share, a year earlier. Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting a profit of $1.81 a share.
Revenue increased to $3.68 billion from $3.05 billion a year prior. Analysts were expecting $3.59 billion in revenue.
Operating expenses grew to $3.43 billion from $2.81 billion a year prior.

J.B. Hunt said last month that strong demand was leading to higher costs as it increases hiring and compensation. It warned investors that the third-quarter profit would fall 5% to 10% from the second quarter.
The company's Thursday results showed that profit was down 4.7% from $181 million in the second quarter.
Shares of J.B. Hunt fell 4.3%, to $255.23, in after-hours trading.
In the company's intermodal business, revenue grew 20%, to $1.83 billion, with volume up 8%.
Revenue from the integrated capacity solutions segment surged 57%, to $434 million. Truckload revenue rose 37%, to $261 million, and dedicated contract services revenue grew 11%, to $960 million.
The final mile services segment had its revenue slide 3%, to $200 million.
